Quad9 to stop serving France after court fine over pirate-streaming domain blocking
Swiss non-profit Quad9, which runs the free 9.9.9.9 DNS resolver, will stop answering DNS queries from France on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The excerpt says a Paris court fined Quad9 for refusing to block a list of pirate sports-streaming domains on behalf of beIN Sports. It also states that around 20 similar cases are pending in France, and Cloudflare called the departure "a canary in the coal mine."

Java4Shell disclosure details critical RCE flaw in OpenJDK Base64 decoder
A disclosure describes Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. The disclosure says it scores 9.2 out of 10 (critical) under CVSS 4.0 and calls OpenJDK the most popular Java runtime.

Nvidia stops shipping licensed Hopper AI chips to China, interim CEO says
The Verge reports that Nvidia has stopped sending its advanced AI chips to China, despite White House approval it received in December last year. Interim CEO Colette Kress said during an earnings call on Tuesday that Nvidia has stopped shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China.

Randomized experiment finds Google AI Overviews cut clicks to websites by about 40%
Researchers hid AI Overviews from some US desktop users in a randomized experiment. Comparing those users with users who still saw Overviews, they found an Overview cut clicks to outside websites by about 40%. The excerpt says Overviews now appear on more than half the US keywords DataForSEO tracks, up from 6% two years ago.

Harvard working paper finds AI coding agents shift bottleneck to code review
A job-market working paper by Harvard Ph.D. candidates Fiona Chen and James Stratton, covering 718 firms, found engineers at firms that adopted AI coding agents added about 30% more code. The same paper found that getting code through review took 49% longer.

LeBron James passes Jason Kidd for third on NBA assists list as Sixers reach 12-3
LeBron James passed Hall of Famer Jason Kidd for third place on the NBA's career assists list in a win over Indiana. His playmaking milestone came during a two-game winning stretch for Philadelphia.

Short-handed Pistons end Spurs’ 12-game streak as Harper limps off with groin injury
Missing four regulars, Detroit came back from 14 down to beat San Antonio 105-93 and end the league-best Spurs streak. The Spurs also lost Dylan Harper, their second-leading scorer, to a groin injury in the final minute, and his status remains unclear.

Jaylen Brown Out Wednesday With Hamstring Strain
Jaylen Brown is set to miss the Philadelphia 76ers' matchup against the Orlando Magic on Wednesday with a left hamstring strain. Brown will be re-evaluated before Saturday's game against the Bucks. Brown suffered the injury late in the fourth quarter of Monday's win over the Nets. Brown is averaging 22.6 points and 6.6 rebounds on the year.

Warriors changes coming after second straight blowout loss without Steph Curry
NEW ORLEANS — When you lose in blowout fashion to a red-hot team that was in the NBA Finals five months ago, that’s one thing. When it’s followed by an almost-as-disastrous defeat to a bottom-of-the-barrel squad that had dropped its past six games, something’s got to give. “Especially in the fashion that we’ve lost,” guard De’Anthony Melton said, “expect things to change. As they should, given the last two losses, how we lost.” Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr looks on during an NBA basketball game against the New Orleans Pelicans in New Orleans, Monday, Nov. 16, 2026. …

Rough Hawks injury news: CJ McCollum out 4 weeks (calf strain), Asa Newell likely out for season (toe)
This is rough injury news for Atlanta, which at 8-6 sits tied for the 4/5 seeds in the East: • Guard CJ McCollum suffered a strained left calf and will be reevaluated in four weeks, the team announced. • Big man Asa Newell has surgery to repair a left great toe hyperextension, and while the Hawks' announcement says he will be re-evaluated in four months, that will be mid-March, weeks away from the end of the regular season (April 11). It's unlikely we see Newell again this season. …

GTA 6 launches to universal critical acclaim; Take-Two shares jump in pre-market trading
After a 13-year wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has been met with universal acclaim, and recent data shows over 17 million pre-orders generating more than $1.6 billion in revenue. GameSpot reports Take-Two shares were up close to 7% in pre-market trading after the reviews landed.

Firaxis lays off about 60 employees, a third of its workforce
Take-Two studio Firaxis, maker of Civilization and the XCOM revivals, is cutting around a third of its workforce, affecting approximately 60 employees. According to Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, a 2K Games spokesperson confirmed that studio head Heather Hazen is leaving.

Build a Rocket Boy plans litigation against alleged "saboteurs" to recoup £61.7m debt
MindsEye developer Build a Rocket Boy owes £61.7 million in debt. It plans to recoup the money by pursuing litigation against alleged "saboteurs".

WoW: Forever hits record launch numbers, with more weekly players than in 15 years
World of Warcraft: Forever had the biggest concurrent player launch in the MMO's history, according to the report. Executive producer Holly Longdale said over 15 million characters have been logged, and that the game has more people playing weekly than Blizzard has seen in 15 years.

Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is the best-selling physical game in the US for 2026
According to Circana's Mat Piscatella, the Ocarina of Time remake became the best-selling physical video game in the US for 2026, selling over one million copies as of November 7th. GamingBolt says Nintendo's remake has sold over 5.2 million copies in four days.

Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI. Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they’re ready to play on launch day, November 19.

Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of China summit
President Trump shook hands with Russian President Putin and Chinese President Xi ahead of talks in China. The three leaders are due to meet together for the first time on Thursday during a closely watched summit, according to Al Jazeera, BBC World and NPR Politics.

Analysts warn US-Iran 'status quo' could break out into war
Iran and the US have continued to exchange strikes in recent days, but all-out war has so far been avoided, according to Al Jazeera and BBC World. Analysts warn the situation could escalate into war.

Israel begins operation in central Gaza as Palestinians flee refugee camp
Palestinians fled a refugee camp as Israel began an operation in central Gaza, Al Jazeera reports. The Israeli army says the operation west of the 'Yellow Line' aims to 'eliminate a threat'.

Ukraine hit Crimean bridge in two waves of strikes after weeks-long operation
Al Jazeera reports that a weeks-long operation was behind two waves of strikes on Putin's prized bridge. The strikes used long-range missiles and drones developed in Ukraine.

Israel delays building contracts for E1 West Bank settlement after UK sanctions
Israel has postponed issuing contracts for building a large West Bank settlement seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, The Guardian reports. The delay came days after the UK imposed sanctions on building firms operating in the area.

This winter, more than 1,000 air defence missiles and over a dozen air defence radars will be delivered to Ukraine as part of a £240 million package. This vital equipment will help strengthen Ukraine's air defences and protect against Russia's relentless attacks.

⚡️️ European Commission approves proposal to provide additional $49.5 billion to Ukraine.

The European Commission on Nov. 18 approved a set of legislative proposals to provide up to €45 billion ($49.5 billion) in additional financial support to Ukraine in 2027.

The Kremlin says Putin briefed Xi Jinping on the war in Ukraine. Peskov confirmed Ukraine will dominate Putin's discussions with Trump and Xi at the summit in China. A formal Putin-Trump meeting now appears unlikely, while work continues on a joint trilateral statement. #Ukraine

Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate seat, beating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan
Democrat Mary Peltola defeated Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in the Alaska Senate race, according to Al Jazeera, BBC World and NPR Politics. The excerpt says it was the last U.S. Senate contest resolved in this year's midterm elections and that Democrats flipped nine GOP-held seats to retake the chamber.

Republicans could expedite bill to make big oil immune to lawsuits, warn experts
The Guardian US reports that GOP lawmakers are rushing high-priority bills before newly elected Democrats are sworn in. Climate groups fear a bill could pass by the end of the year giving fossil fuel companies immunity from lawsuits and from legislation holding them accountable for the climate crisis, and hundreds of elected leaders and climate groups urged Democratic leadership to reject any such proposal.

US loses long-held measles elimination status, according to PAHO declaration
The Pan American Health Organization declared measles resurgent in the United States, Bolivia and Mexico on Tuesday, meaning the virus has spread continuously for 12 months, according to The Guardian US. Public health leaders quoted by the outlet expressed grief and alarm and condemned what they called significant damage by the Trump administration.

Florida labels CAIR a terrorist organization, prompting lawsuit from CAIR-Florida
Under a new process, Florida designated the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) a domestic terrorist organization, according to The Guardian US. CAIR-Florida is suing state officials, and the outlet reports the designation meant the group had to shut its doors to victims of harassment and discrimination.

White House withdraws nomination of Heidi Overton to lead FDA
The White House has dropped its nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration, a White House official told The Guardian US. Trump nominated Overton, a physician and prominent abortion opponent, in August, and the withdrawal came a day before a key Senate health committee vote.
